title: Adoption by the main product: DCLab's decision classifiers read as its R3 reads a model
request: The classifiers as a DCLab answerer in the main product's own path for custom decision models: the same purposes and state, rows shaped like its answer table, R3 runs on its side; decision datasets exported in its label format under consent. Done when the mapping is a tested adapter in dclab_core and an R3-shaped run on generated cases compares a classifier with the rule.
spec: An adapter in dclab_core reading the main product's release fields, answer tuple, bands, level-2 policy, metrics and digests at one commit; a runner on generated dev cases; the label export through consent.
plan: Survey what exists and the main product's R3 and releases at the recorded commit.
Record the release fields and the R3 fields.
Write the answerer, the reading, the rows and the export.
Run on generated dev cases, review against the main product's code, plant faults, fix, run again.

decisions.decision: Each classifier is read twice: on the state as trained and on the state the main product sends.
decisions.why: The main product sends fewer fields; what that costs is part of the answer.

decisions.decision: The wiring there, the invocation row and the ADR are said as the main product's changes.
decisions.why: Its repository is never changed from here.

decisions.decision: Only dev rows of the generated sets.
decisions.why: Their sealed rows were read once by 22.3.

change: dclab_core/adapters/main_product_r3.py (new), main_product_ledger.py (as_raw, to_semantic_answer), main_product_fields.json (releases, r3), dclab_rnd/decision_r3.py (new), consent.py (export_main_product), Makefile, docs/guides/CORE_INTEGRATION.md, dclab-core 0.34.0; tests/test_main_product_r3.py (new); the plan, the roadmap, CLAUDE.md.

findings.defect: The answer row wrote a classifier's confident no as a yes.
findings.scenario: A classifier answering no at 0.97 was written with the value 0.97, which the main product reads as the probability of yes.
findings.cause: The classifier's confidence went where the main product reads a probability of yes.
findings.fix: A yes or no is the probability of yes; a choice is its label; the band and the agreement are the main product's.

findings.defect: The level-2 policy let a role model override where the main product does not.
findings.scenario: Rule categorical_code, model identifier in its band: DCLab used the model, the main product keeps the rule; the stored role gap was 2 points too high.
findings.fix: A model overrides at semantic_role only between numeric and categorical_code, and only a value the validator accepts; the run was redone.

findings.defect: Inside the main product's harness the column name was lost.
findings.scenario: Its cases keep the column apart from the fields, so the role and leakage classifiers answered without the name.
findings.cause: The answerer read the fields and context only.
findings.fix: The column is read from the case.

findings.defect: Label rows broke the main product's supersede rules.
findings.scenario: Two labels on one decision both superseded the answer row, a unique index there; a measured label left a version 2 without a version 1.
findings.cause: Every label pointed at the record and versions were numbered before dropping.
findings.fix: Versions after dropping, each label superseding the one before, a time required, the answer row's columns copied.

findings.defect: The metrics had the main product's names and other definitions.
findings.scenario: With half the answers unavailable the gap was half the main product's and the rates halved.
findings.cause: Statistics over every case and a two-sided bootstrap.
findings.fix: Every statistic on answered cases, rates over answered cases, one-sided bounds by cluster as there, per-band precision.

findings.defect: The run row could not be loaded there.
findings.scenario: The report had no run id, time or digests, so its verification would call it tampered; long values were sliced.
findings.cause: The report was built without the fields the main product verifies.
findings.fix: The report carries its run id, time and digests computed as there; long values are refused.

findings.defect: An answer without a value became a no, and a plain yes was out of band.
findings.scenario: A classifier answer with no value was written as probability 0; a model's plain True was not in the band there.
findings.cause: No value was read as a no; a bool was not read as a probability.
findings.fix: No value is no answer; a plain yes or no is a probability of 1 or 0.

findings.scenario: A planted fault that never checked the ai_off arm passed every test.
findings.cause: With no model the policy is the rule by construction.
findings.fix: A test gives the off arm answers and expects the ablation to fail.

measurements.name: an R3-shaped run of the classifiers against the rule
measurements.gate: an R3-shaped run on generated cases compares a classifier with the rule
measurements.result: on 600 generated dev cases per purpose, the role classifier's gap over the rule +0.0617 as trained and +0.0633 as sent; leakage +0.045 as trained and +0.0283 as sent with 22 in its band; identifier -0.05 as sent; the ablation holds
measurements.against_gate: the comparison made for each of the three purposes
limits: Generated cases whose rule is the data card's.
The main product's gates need its blind labels.

measurements.name: planted faults
measurements.gate: each planted fault fails a test
measurements.result: 14 of 14 planted faults caught after one test was added

outcome: A DCLab decision classifier answers in the main product's R3 shape and is read here as it would be read there; the answer row no longer turns a classifier's no into a yes.
lessons: Read the other side's scoring before naming metrics after it: the same names hid other definitions.
An adapter's tests must use the other side's shapes, not one's own: the column lived apart in its cases.
A confidence is not a probability of yes.
risks: The wiring, the invocation row and the ADR are the main product's changes.
The leakage classifier sees no availability here.
